lean.signature:
structure ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.{u} (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Type u where
  fct : (k : ℕ) → (Fin k → ℝ) → X → ℝ
  continuous_fct : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin k → ℝ), Continuous[inst✝, _] (fct k y)
lean.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme
lean.docstring:
An **adaptive scheme of continuous measurements** on `X`.

After `k` values `y : Fin k → ℝ` have been observed, the next functional to be
evaluated is `fct k y : X → ℝ`.  Each such functional is continuous in the point
being measured; the dependence of `fct k y` on `y` is arbitrary, and that dependence
is precisely what "adaptive" means.

The scheme carries no length: a scheme of any length is obtained by reading off only
the first `n` measurements, see `AdaptiveScheme.info`.

lean.signature:
def ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.DistinguishesAntipodes.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [Neg X]
  (S : AdaptiveScheme X) (n : ℕ) (K : Set X) : Prop
lean.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.DistinguishesAntipodes
lean.docstring:
A scheme **distinguishes antipodes** on `K` with `n` measurements if the
information map separates every antipodal pair of `K`.

This is the property that an algorithm with small error forces: if
`dist x (Φ (N x)) < R` for all `x` on the sphere of radius `R`, then `N x = N (-x)`
would put the two antipodes, which are `2R` apart, at distance `< R` from a common
point.  The lower bound therefore consists in showing that `n` measurements cannot
distinguish antipodes unless `2ⁿ ≥ dim X + 1`.

lean.signature:
def ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) :
  AdaptiveScheme X → X → Fin n → ℝ
lean.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info
lean.docstring:
The **information map** `N : X → ℝⁿ` of the first `n` measurements of a scheme:
`N x = (λ₁ x, λ₂^{(y₁)} x, …)`, each functional being selected by the values already
produced.

The recursion peels off the first measurement, so what changes in the recursive call
is the scheme, not the point.

lean.signature: def ContMeasurements.minMeasurements.{u_2} (E : Type u_2) [NormedAddCommGroup E] (R ε : ℝ) : ℕ
lean.name: ContMeasurements.minMeasurements
lean.docstring:
The least number of adaptive continuous measurements that suffice to recover every
vector of the closed ball of radius `R` to within `ε`.

Only the norm of `E` enters, so no scalar action is assumed here; the bounds below add
what they need.

`Nat.sInf` returns `0` when no such number exists; those bounds always come with
hypotheses that exclude this.

lean.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.DistinguishesAntipodes.hasSplitCover
lean.docstring:
**The covering proposition.**  If `n` adaptive continuous measurements distinguish
all antipodal pairs of a compact symmetric set `K`, then `K` is covered by `2ⁿ - 1`
split sets.

The proof is the induction described in the module docstring; it uses no topology
beyond compactness, and in particular **no** Borsuk–Ulam.

lean.signature:
theorem hasSplitCover_two_mul_of_forall_fiber.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {Z : Set E}
  {μ : E → ℝ} {h : ℕ} (hZ : IsCompact Z) (hsymm : ∀ x ∈ Z, -x ∈ Z) (hμ : Continuous μ)
  (hμeven : ∀ x ∈ Z, μ (-x) = μ x) (hlevel : ∀ (y : ℝ), HasSplitCover (Z ∩ μ ⁻¹' {y}) h) :
  HasSplitCover Z (2 * h)
lean.name: hasSplitCover_two_mul_of_forall_fiber
lean.docstring:
**Halving lemma.** If every level set of an even continuous function `μ` on a
compact symmetric set `Z` is covered by `h` split sets, then `Z` is covered by `2h`
split sets.

One real value therefore costs a factor of two, and this is sharp.

lean.signature: def HasSplitCover.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (K : Set E) (k : ℕ) : Prop
lean.name: HasSplitCover
lean.docstring:
`HasSplitCover K k` : the set `K` can be covered by `k` split sets, each given by
its positive half `P i`.

nodes.title: Split cover on preimages of balls

lean.signature:
theorem HasSplitCover.exists_pos_inter_preimage_ball.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {Z : Set E}
  {μ : E → ℝ} {h : ℕ} (hZ : IsCompact Z) (hsymm : ∀ x ∈ Z, -x ∈ Z) (hμ : Continuous μ)
  (hμeven : ∀ x ∈ Z, μ (-x) = μ x) (y : ℝ) (hlevel : HasSplitCover (Z ∩ μ ⁻¹' {y}) h) :
  ∃ ρ > 0, HasSplitCover (Z ∩ μ ⁻¹' Metric.ball y ρ) h
lean.name: HasSplitCover.exists_pos_inter_preimage_ball
lean.docstring:
**From a level set to a slab.**

If the level set `Z ∩ μ⁻¹{y}` of an even function `μ` admits a cover by `h` split
sets, then so does `Z ∩ μ⁻¹(B(y, ρ))` for some `ρ > 0`.

The proof fattens the split sets of the level set to a closed neighbourhood of it
(`HasSplitCover.exists_cthickening`), and then uses compactness: the points of `Z` that
stay away from the level set have `μ`-values bounded away from `y`, because their
image is compact and misses `y`.

nodes.title: Split cover gives an odd map without zeros

lean.signature:
theorem HasSplitCover.exists_odd_continuous_ne_zero.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {K : Set E}
  {k : ℕ} (hc : HasSplitCover K k) : ∃ Ψ, Continuous Ψ ∧ Function.Odd Ψ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, Ψ x ≠ 0
lean.name: HasSplitCover.exists_odd_continuous_ne_zero
lean.docstring:
**From a split cover to an odd map without zeros.**

Given `k` split sets covering `K`, the sign functions
`σ_i(x) = dist(x, -(P i)) - dist(x, P i)` assemble into a continuous odd map
`Ψ : E → ℝᵏ` that vanishes nowhere on `K`: each `x ∈ K` lies in some split set, and
there `σ_i(x) ≠ 0` because the two halves are closed and disjoint.

Together with the Borsuk–Ulam theorem this converts a covering count into a dimension
bound.

nodes.title: One split set from an odd function

lean.name: hasSplitCover_one_of_odd_ne_zero
lean.docstring:
A closed symmetric set on which a continuous **odd** function has no zero is a
single split set: the sign of the function tells `x` from `-x`.

This is the elementary engine of the lower bound.  Applied to
`δ(x) = λ(x) - λ(-x)`, the odd part of a measurement `λ`, it says that wherever the
measurement actually separates an antipodal pair, one split set settles the matter.

lean.name: HasSplitCover.exists_cthickening
lean.docstring:
**Fattening.** A split cover of a compact symmetric set survives passing to a
closed neighbourhood of it: the halves are thickened by less than half their mutual
distance, so they stay disjoint.

This is what lets the induction of the lower bound cover, not just a level set, but a
whole slab around it.

lean.signature:
theorem HasSplitCover.biUnion_of_pairwise_disjoint.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {ι : Type u_2} {s : Finset ι} {Z : ι → Set E} {h : ℕ} (hZc : ∀ j ∈ s, IsCompact (Z j))
  (hZs : ∀ j ∈ s, ∀ x ∈ Z j, -x ∈ Z j) (hZd : ∀ j ∈ s, ∀ j' ∈ s, j ≠ j' → Disjoint (Z j) (Z j'))
  (hZ : ∀ j ∈ s, HasSplitCover (Z j) h) : HasSplitCover (⋃ j ∈ s, Z j) h
lean.name: HasSplitCover.biUnion_of_pairwise_disjoint
lean.docstring:
**Pairwise disjoint pieces share their split sets.**

If compact symmetric sets `Z j` are pairwise disjoint and each is covered by `h`
split sets, then their union is covered by `h` split sets, not by `h` times the
number of pieces.  The `i`-th split set of the union is the union of the `i`-th split
sets of the pieces; it is again split because a point and its reflection lie in the
same piece.

Applied to the slabs of a measurement's level sets, this is exactly the step that
costs only a factor `2` (odd-numbered slabs and even-numbered slabs each form a
disjoint family).

lean.signature:
theorem ContMeasurements.exists_norm_eq_and_info_eq_info_neg.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

the `n` continuous measurements are chosen, adaptively and with no regularity in the
observed values, some antipodal pair on the sphere of radius `R` produces exactly the
same information.

adaptivity moves it to `log₂ m`, and by the recovery algorithm of `UpperBound.lean`
no further.

lean.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.DistinguishesAntipodes.finrank_add_one_le_two_pow
lean.docstring:
The counting form of the lower bound: `n` adaptive continuous measurements that
separate every antipodal pair of a sphere in a `d`-dimensional normed space satisfy
`2ⁿ ≥ d + 1`, that is `n ≥ ⌈log₂(d+1)⌉`.

Holds for **any** norm and any radius `R > 0`.

**The lower bound in the form used for complexity.**  If `2ⁿ ≤ dim E`, then every
algorithm built from `n` adaptive continuous measurements and an arbitrary
reconstruction map `Φ` errs by at least `R` at some point of the sphere of radius `R`.

In words: below `log₂(dim E)` measurements nothing at all can be achieved, since the
error is no better than that of the trivial algorithm returning the centre.

lean.signature:
theorem borsukUlam {m k : ℕ} (hk : k < m) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) → Fin k → ℝ)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Metric.sphere 0 1)) (hodd : Function.Odd f) :
  ∃ x ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1, f x = 0
lean.name: borsukUlam
lean.docstring:
**Borsuk–Ulam theorem** (odd-map form).  A map into `ℝᵏ` with `k < m` that is odd
and continuous on the unit sphere of `ℝᵐ` vanishes at some point of that sphere.

Equivalently: `k < m` continuous functionals cannot separate all antipodal pairs of
`S^{m-1}`.

The Euclidean sphere is reached from the sphere of the sup norm by projecting radially
along a linear homeomorphism, which is odd and continuous away from the origin.

lean.signature:
theorem borsukUlam_cube {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (g : (Fin n → ℝ) → Fin n → ℝ)
  (hg : ContinuousOn g (Metric.closedBall 0 1))
  (hodd : ∀ (x : Fin n → ℝ), ‖x‖ = 1 → g (-x) = -g x) : ∃ x ∈ Metric.closedBall 0 1, g x = 0
lean.name: borsukUlam_cube
lean.docstring:
**Borsuk's antipodal theorem, cube form.**

A map of the cube `[-1, 1]ⁿ` into `ℝⁿ` that is continuous on the cube and odd on its
boundary vanishes somewhere in the cube.  Here `Fin n → ℝ` carries the sup norm, so the
closed unit ball is the cube and the unit sphere is its boundary.

The proof is Tucker's lemma plus uniform continuity.  If the map never vanished, its norm
would have a positive minimum `ε` on the compact cube.  Choose a mesh `1 / N` below the
modulus of continuity for `2 * ε` and label each grid point of `[-N, N]ⁿ` by the
coordinate in which its image is largest, together with the sign there.  Oddness on the
boundary makes this labelling antipodal, so Tucker's lemma gives two neighbouring grid
points whose labels are opposite.  Their images then differ by at least `2 * ε` in one
coordinate, although the points are closer than the mesh.

lean.signature:
theorem Function.Odd.exists_norm_eq_and_eq_zero_of_lt_finrank.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {m k : ℕ} (hm : Module.finrank ℝ E = m) (hk : k < m)
  {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (Ψ : E → Fin k → ℝ) (hΨc : Continuous Ψ) (hΨo : Function.Odd Ψ) :
  ∃ x, ‖x‖ = R ∧ Ψ x = 0
lean.name: Function.Odd.exists_norm_eq_and_eq_zero_of_lt_finrank
lean.docstring:
**Borsuk–Ulam for an arbitrary norm and an arbitrary radius.**

On a real normed space of finite dimension `m`, every continuous odd map
`Ψ : E → ℝᵏ` with `k < m` vanishes at some point of norm `R`, for every `R > 0`.

The reduction to the Euclidean unit sphere is purely formal: a linear homeomorphism
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) ≃L[ℝ] E` carries the Euclidean unit sphere onto a compact
symmetric set, and the radial map `u ↦ (R / ‖e u‖) • e u` sends it onto the sphere of
radius `R` of `E` oddly and continuously.  No property of the norm of `E` is used
beyond homogeneity, which is why the lower bound holds for *any* norm.

lean.signature:
theorem borsukUlam_pi {m k : ℕ} (hk : k < m) (f : (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin k → ℝ)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Metric.sphere 0 1)) (hodd : Function.Odd f) :
  ∃ x ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1, f x = 0
lean.name: borsukUlam_pi
lean.docstring:
**Borsuk–Ulam theorem for the sup norm.**

A map into `ℝᵏ` with `k < m` that is odd and continuous on the unit sphere of
`Fin m → ℝ`, taken with the sup norm, vanishes at some point of that sphere.

The unit sphere of the sup norm is the boundary of the cube one dimension lower, reached
by `CubeSphere.proj`; padding the values with zeros to `m - 1` coordinates turns the
statement into `borsukUlam_cube`.

**A simplex with as many vertices as directions and one extremal coordinate has exactly

lean.signature:
structure GridSimplex.IsSimplex {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (s : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)) : Prop where
  nonempty : s.Nonempty
  subset_grid : s ⊆ GridSimplex.grid n N
  chain : IsChain (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2) ↑s
  sub_le_one : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ (i : Fin n), y i - x i ≤ 1
lean.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex
lean.docstring:
A simplex of the Kuhn triangulation of the grid: a nonempty set of grid points that is
a chain for the coordinatewise order and whose points differ by at most one in every
coordinate.

These are exactly the faces of the triangulation; a top-dimensional one is a chain
`v < v + e_{i₁} < v + e_{i₁} + e_{i₂} < …`.

lean.signature:
theorem GridSimplex.tucker {n N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (lam : (Fin n → ℤ) → GridSimplex.Label n)
  (hlam :
    ∀ v ∈ GridSimplex.grid n N,
      GridSimplex.IsBoundary N v → lam (-v) = GridSimplex.negLabel (lam v)) :
  ∃ u ∈ GridSimplex.grid n N,
    ∃ w ∈ GridSimplex.grid n N,
      u ≤ w ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n), w i - u i ≤ 1) ∧ lam u = GridSimplex.negLabel (lam w)
lean.name: GridSimplex.tucker
lean.docstring:
**Tucker's lemma.**

Label every point of the integer cube `[-N, N]ⁿ` by a coordinate together with a sign, so
that antipodal boundary points get opposite labels.  Then two points of one simplex of the
Kuhn triangulation carry opposite labels.

The proof counts the doors between happy simplices in two ways.  All but two kinds of
happy simplex have exactly two doors; the exceptions are the origin alone and the
simplices with one coordinate at the boundary of the cube, and reflection in the origin
pairs the latter up.  So the number of happy simplices of odd degree is odd, while
counting the doors from both ends makes it even.

theorem ContMeasurements.exists_bisection_scheme.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [Nonempty X]

**Bisection over colors.**

Given, for each color `r`, a scheme of `ℓ` measurements together with a
reconstruction map that is `η`-accurate on `closure (A r)`, and a finite set `C` of at
most `2ᴸ` colors, there is a scheme of `ℓ + L` measurements together with a
reconstruction map that is `η`-accurate on `closure (⋃ r ∈ C, A r)`.

The `L` extra measurements are the bisection steps that identify a color.

both the diameter bound and the separation constant are multiplied by `s`.

small diameter, which is what turns the recovery algorithm into one of arbitrary
accuracy.

LebesgueCover.exists_int_abs_sub_le_of_n.name: LebesgueCover.exists_int_abs_sub_le_of_ne
LebesgueCover.exists_int_abs_sub_le_of_n.docstring:
**The geometric heart of the construction.**

If a point `x` is close to two *distinct* faces of the same dimension `k`, then one of
the directions `i₀` spanned by the first face carries an integer very near `x i₀`.
Replacing that coordinate of the first face by the integer produces a point of the
`(k-1)`-skeleton just as close to `x`, which is what the construction of the pieces
has excluded.

The bound `δ + δ' < 1` is what makes the argument work: two lattice points that differ
must differ by at least `1`.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_lt_of_insert.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_lt_of_insert
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_lt_of_insert.docstring:
If the enlarged simplex has no more directions than the total step set has
coordinates, no vertex can be added below the least one.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_gt_of_insert.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_gt_of_insert
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_gt_of_insert.docstring:
If the enlarged simplex has no more directions than the total step set has
coordinates, no vertex can be added above the greatest one.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_between_of_sat.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_between_of_saturated
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.not_between_of_sat.docstring: A saturated simplex admits no new vertex between its least and its greatest.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.neg.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.neg
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.neg.docstring: The reflection of a simplex in the origin is a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.lt_of_rank_lt.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.lt_of_rank_lt
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.lt_of_rank_lt.docstring: The rank reflects the order: a vertex of smaller rank is smaller.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_vertex.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_vertex
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_vertex.docstring:
Inserting a vertex that is comparable with every vertex of a simplex and differs from
each by at most one in every coordinate again gives a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_raise.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_raise
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_raise.docstring: Inserting the greatest vertex with one constant coordinate raised gives a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_lower.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_lower
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_lower.docstring: Inserting the least vertex with one constant coordinate lowered gives a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_between.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_between
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.insert_between.docstring: Inserting a vertex between two consecutive vertices gives a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.injOn_rank.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.injOn_rank
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.injOn_rank.docstring: The rank is injective on a simplex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.image_rank.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.image_rank
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.image_rank.docstring: A saturated simplex realises every rank up to the size of its total step set.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_top.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_top
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_top.docstring: A simplex has a greatest vertex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_step_eq_ins.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_step_eq_insert
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_step_eq_ins.docstring:
In a saturated simplex, the step set of the successor of a vertex adds exactly one
coordinate.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_rank_eq.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_rank_eq
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_rank_eq.docstring: Hence every rank below the size of the total step set occurs at a vertex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_top_add_.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_top_add_single
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_top_add_.docstring: A vertex above the whole simplex is one unit step above its greatest vertex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_sing.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_single_bot
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_sing.docstring: A vertex below the whole simplex is one unit step below its least vertex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_sing.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_single
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_eq_add_sing.docstring: **Consecutive vertices of a saturated simplex differ by one unit step.**

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_bot.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_bot
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.exists_bot.docstring: A simplex has a least vertex.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_or_eq_add_one.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_or_eq_add_one
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_or_eq_add_one.docstring:
Measured from the least vertex, every coordinate of every vertex is either the base
value or one more.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_add_ite.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_add_ite
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.eq_add_ite.docstring: Every vertex is the least vertex raised by one in the coordinates of its step set.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_to.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_top
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_to.docstring: A vertex added above a simplex raises a coordinate that is constant on it.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_bo.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_bot
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.const_of_insert_bo.docstring: A vertex added below a simplex lowers a coordinate that is constant on it.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_signs.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_signs
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_signs.docstring:
On the signs of a simplex the coordinate determines the label, so a simplex has as many
signs as directions.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_step_.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_step_succ
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_step_.docstring:
**A simplex has at most one more vertex than its total step set has coordinates.**

The rank is injective on the simplex and takes values between `0` and the number of
coordinates in which the greatest vertex exceeds the least one.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_direc.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_directions_succ
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_le_card_direc.docstring:
**A simplex has at most one more vertex than it has directions.**

Every coordinate in which the greatest vertex exceeds the least one is a direction.

GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_eq_card_step_.name: GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_eq_card_step_succ
GridSimplex.IsSimplex.card_eq_card_step_.docstring:
A simplex with one more vertex than it has directions is saturated: every direction is
already a coordinate in which the greatest vertex exceeds the least one.

GridSimplex.IsHappy.shape.name: GridSimplex.IsHappy.shape
GridSimplex.IsHappy.shape.docstring:
**The three shapes of a happy simplex.**

Writing `k` for the number of directions, a happy simplex has either `k + 1` vertices and
`k + 1` labels, or `k + 1` vertices and `k` labels, or `k` vertices and `k` labels.

GridSimplex.IsHappy.labels_eq_signs.name: GridSimplex.IsHappy.labels_eq_signs
GridSimplex.IsHappy.labels_eq_signs.docstring: A happy simplex with as many labels as directions carries exactly its signs.

GridSimplex.IsHappy.exists_extra_label.name: GridSimplex.IsHappy.exists_extra_label
GridSimplex.IsHappy.exists_extra_label.docstring:
A happy simplex with one more label than directions carries exactly one label beyond
its signs.

GridSimplex.IsHappy.card_directions_le.name: GridSimplex.IsHappy.card_directions_le
GridSimplex.IsHappy.card_directions_le.docstring: A happy simplex has at least as many labels as directions.

GridSimplex.IsHappy.name: GridSimplex.IsHappy
GridSimplex.IsHappy.docstring:
A simplex is **happy** for a labelling when every sign it carries occurs as a label on
it.  The parity argument runs over the happy simplices.

GridSimplex.IsExtremal.neg_ne.name: GridSimplex.IsExtremal.neg_ne
GridSimplex.IsExtremal.neg_ne.docstring:
**Reflection has no fixed extremal face.**  An extremal face and its reflection differ,
because the extreme coordinate would have to take both values `N` and `-N`.

GridSimplex.IsExtremal.name: GridSimplex.IsExtremal
GridSimplex.IsExtremal.docstring: One coordinate is constantly `N`, or constantly `-N`, on `s`.

GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_right.name: GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_right
GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_right.docstring: The larger end of a door is happy.

GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_left.name: GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_left
GridSimplex.IsDoor.happy_left.docstring: The smaller end of a door is happy.

GridSimplex.IsDoor.name: GridSimplex.IsDoor
GridSimplex.IsDoor.docstring:
`σ` is a **door** of `τ`: it is `τ` with one vertex deleted, still nonempty, and it
already carries every sign of `τ`.

GridSimplex.IsBoundary.name: GridSimplex.IsBoundary
GridSimplex.IsBoundary.docstring:
A grid point lies on the boundary of the cube when one of its coordinates is
extremal.

Finset.even_card_of_involutive.name: Finset.even_card_of_involutive
Finset.even_card_of_involutive.docstring:
**A finite set carrying a fixed-point-free involution has even cardinality.**  Its
elements fall into pairs.

CubeSphere.proj_neg_of_norm_eq_one.name: CubeSphere.proj_neg_of_norm_eq_one
CubeSphere.proj_neg_of_norm_eq_one.docstring: On the boundary of the cube the projection is odd.

CubeSphere.proj.name: CubeSphere.proj
CubeSphere.proj.docstring: The radial projection of the lift onto the unit sphere of `ℝ^{n+1}`.

CubeSphere.norm_proj.name: CubeSphere.norm_proj
CubeSphere.norm_proj.docstring: The projection lands on the unit sphere.

CubeSphere.norm_lift_pos.name: CubeSphere.norm_lift_pos
CubeSphere.norm_lift_pos.docstring: The lift is never the origin.

CubeSphere.norm_le_norm_lift.name: CubeSphere.norm_le_norm_lift
CubeSphere.norm_le_norm_lift.docstring: Lifting does not decrease the sup norm.

CubeSphere.lift_neg_of_norm_eq_one.name: CubeSphere.lift_neg_of_norm_eq_one
CubeSphere.lift_neg_of_norm_eq_one.docstring: On the boundary of the cube the slack vanishes, so the lift is odd there.

CubeSphere.lift_last.name: CubeSphere.lift_last
CubeSphere.lift_last.docstring: The last coordinate of the lift is the slack of the sup norm.

CubeSphere.lift_castSucc.name: CubeSphere.lift_castSucc
CubeSphere.lift_castSucc.docstring: The lift keeps the original coordinates.

CubeSphere.lift.name: CubeSphere.lift
CubeSphere.lift.docstring:
The lift of a point of `ℝⁿ` to `ℝ^{n+1}`: its own coordinates, with the slack of its
sup norm as the last one.

CubeSphere.half_le_norm_lift.name: CubeSphere.half_le_norm_lift
CubeSphere.half_le_norm_lift.docstring:
**The lift never comes near the origin.**  Either the point itself is large, or its
slack is.

CubeSphere.continuous_proj.name: CubeSphere.continuous_proj
CubeSphere.continuous_proj.docstring: The projection is continuous, because the lift stays away from the origin.

CubeSphere.abs_one_sub_norm_le.name: CubeSphere.abs_one_sub_norm_le
CubeSphere.abs_one_sub_norm_le.docstring: The slack is bounded by the norm of the lift.

CubeLabel.norm_le_of_label_true.name: CubeLabel.norm_le_of_label_true
CubeLabel.norm_le_of_label_true.docstring: A positively labelled point attains its sup norm there with a positive sign.

CubeLabel.maxIdx_neg.name: CubeLabel.maxIdx_neg
CubeLabel.maxIdx_neg.docstring: Reflection does not move the chosen coordinate.

CubeLabel.maxIdx_mem.name: CubeLabel.maxIdx_mem
CubeLabel.maxIdx_mem.docstring: The chosen coordinate is a largest one.

CubeLabel.maxIdx.name: CubeLabel.maxIdx
CubeLabel.maxIdx.docstring: The least coordinate in which `y` attains its sup norm.

CubeLabel.maxCoords_nonempty.name: CubeLabel.maxCoords_nonempty
CubeLabel.maxCoords_nonempty.docstring: Some coordinate attains the sup norm.

CubeLabel.maxCoords_neg.name: CubeLabel.maxCoords_neg
CubeLabel.maxCoords_neg.docstring: Reflection does not move the largest coordinates.

CubeLabel.maxCoords.name: CubeLabel.maxCoords
CubeLabel.maxCoords.docstring: The coordinates in which `y` attains its sup norm.

CubeLabel.le_neg_norm_of_label_false.name: CubeLabel.le_neg_norm_of_label_false
CubeLabel.le_neg_norm_of_label_false.docstring: A negatively labelled point attains its sup norm there with a negative sign.

CubeLabel.label_neg.name: CubeLabel.label_neg
CubeLabel.label_neg.docstring: **Reflection reverses the label**, away from the origin.

CubeLabel.label.name: CubeLabel.label
CubeLabel.label.docstring:
The label of a point: the least coordinate of largest absolute value, together with
its sign.

CubeLabel.abs_maxIdx.name: CubeLabel.abs_maxIdx
CubeLabel.abs_maxIdx.docstring: At the chosen coordinate the absolute value is the sup norm.

CubeLabel.abs_eq_norm_of_mem.name: CubeLabel.abs_eq_norm_of_mem
CubeLabel.abs_eq_norm_of_mem.docstring: At a largest coordinate the absolute value is the sup norm.

ContMeasurements.lt_of_collar_ne_zero.name: ContMeasurements.lt_of_collar_ne_zero
ContMeasurements.lt_of_collar_ne_zero.docstring: The only way the collar can be nonzero is close to the set.

ContMeasurements.locallyFinite_identifyT.name: ContMeasurements.locallyFinite_identifyTerm
ContMeasurements.locallyFinite_identifyT.docstring:
Near any point, at most one piece of the color `r` contributes a nonzero term:
two of them would be closer than the separation constant `c`.

ContMeasurements.identify_eq.name: ContMeasurements.identify_eq
ContMeasurements.identify_eq.docstring:
**The value of the identification functional.**  At a point within `c/8` of the
piece `i` of color `r`, the functional takes the value `e i + 1`; every other piece
of the same color is too far away to contribute.

ContMeasurements.identifyTerm.name: ContMeasurements.identifyTerm
ContMeasurements.identifyTerm.docstring:
The contribution of the piece `i` to the identification functional: the label
`e i + 1` damped by the collar, and `0` unless the piece is nonempty and has the
color under consideration.

The nonemptiness guard matters: `Metric.infDist x ∅ = 0`, so without it an empty
piece would contribute its full label everywhere.

ContMeasurements.exists_mem_of_identifyT.name: ContMeasurements.exists_mem_of_identifyTerm_ne_zero
ContMeasurements.exists_mem_of_identifyT.docstring:
If the term of a piece is nonzero somewhere in a small ball, the piece comes
close to the centre of that ball.

ContMeasurements.decodePoint_mem.name: ContMeasurements.decodePoint_mem
ContMeasurements.decodePoint_mem.docstring: The decoder applied to the label of a nonempty piece returns a point of that piece.

ContMeasurements.decodePoint.name: ContMeasurements.decodePoint
ContMeasurements.decodePoint.docstring:
The decoder: from the value `n = e i + 1` of the identification functional it
returns some point of the piece `i`.

ContMeasurements.continuous_identifyTerm.name: ContMeasurements.continuous_identifyTerm
ContMeasurements.continuous_identifyTerm.docstring: Each term of the sum is continuous.

ContMeasurements.continuous_identify.name: ContMeasurements.continuous_identify
ContMeasurements.continuous_identify.docstring:
The identification functional is continuous: a locally finite sum of continuous
terms.

ContMeasurements.collar_eq_zero.name: ContMeasurements.collar_eq_zero
ContMeasurements.collar_eq_zero.docstring: The collar vanishes from distance `c/4` on.

ContMeasurements.collar_eq_one.name: ContMeasurements.collar_eq_one
ContMeasurements.collar_eq_one.docstring: The collar equals `1` up to distance `c/8`.

ContMeasurements.collar.name: ContMeasurements.collar
ContMeasurements.collar.docstring: A continuous collar: `1` on `[0, c/8]`, `0` from `c/4` on, values in `[0,1]`.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_com.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_comap
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_com.docstring: Transport commutes with taking the tail.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_bra.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_branch
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail_bra.docstring: After the first value `y` is observed, a branching scheme continues with `choice y`.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.tail.docstring:
The scheme governing the remaining measurements once the value `y` has been
observed: its `k`-th functional is the `(k+1)`-st functional of `S`, asked after the
values `y, ys`.

This is the formal content of the informal step "on a set where the first answer is
constant, the algorithm continues with one measurement less"; the crucial point for
the lower bound is that `S.tail y` depends only on the *value* `y`, so two points
producing the same first answer face literally the same continuation.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_suc.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_succ
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_suc.docstring: Unfolding one measurement: the first value, then the information of the tail scheme.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_con.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_const_one
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_con.docstring: One measurement of `const f hf` returns the value of `f`.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_com.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_comap
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_com.docstring: The information of a transported scheme is the original information at the image point.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_bra.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_branch_succ
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.info_bra.docstring: Information of a branching scheme: `f x`, then the information of the chosen continuation.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_co.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_comap
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_co.docstring: The first functional of a transported scheme.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_br.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_branch
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first_br.docstring: The first functional of a branching scheme is the branching functional.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.first.docstring: The first functional `λ₁` of a scheme, asked before anything has been observed.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.continuo.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.continuous_first
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.continuo.docstring: The first functional of a scheme is continuous.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.const.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.const
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.const.docstring:
The scheme that asks the same functional `f` over and over. Only its first
measurement is ever used, through `info_const_one`.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.comap.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.comap
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.comap.docstring:
Transport a scheme along a continuous map `π : Y → X`: measure `π y` instead of
`y`.  Used to carry a scheme from a space to another one it is homeomorphic to.

ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.branch.name: ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.branch
ContMeasurements.AdaptiveScheme.branch.docstring:
Ask `f` first, then continue with the scheme `choice y` selected from the observed
value `y = f x`.  The selection rule `choice` is an arbitrary function `ℝ → _`; no
regularity is assumed, and none is available.

This combinator builds every adaptive algorithm in this development: the bisection of
the upper bound branches on `choice`, and `tail_branch` is what lets the lower bound
analyse one measurement at a time.

ColoredCover.dist_inv_smul.name: ColoredCover.dist_inv_smul
ColoredCover.dist_inv_smul.docstring: Scaling two vectors by `s⁻¹` with `s > 0` scales their distance by `s⁻¹`.

ColoredCover.colorClass.name: ColoredCover.colorClass
ColoredCover.colorClass.docstring: The set `E_r` of points of color `r`: the union of all pieces colored `r`.
